symptom: `create external entity M.Order from consumed odata service M.Sales (EntitySet: 'Orders') (OrderId: Long, Title: String(100), Status: …)` passed check and exec; mx check 11.12.6 reported CE6010 "Key cannot be empty", CE6612 on every attribute and CE6630 for $top and $skip, on a contract `create external entities` builds at 0 errors.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_odata_single_contract.go resolveSingleExternalEntity (called from execCreateExternalEntity in cmd_odata.go); the per-entity build extracted from the bulk import as contractEntityAttributes (cmd_contract.go); deferred enumerations in cmd_contract_enums.go. Test: mdl/executor/create_external_entity_contract_2497_test.go
cause: The single form built attributes from the statement alone (DomainModels$StoredValue, no RemoteName/RemoteType), wrote no key, and took capabilities from the statement with false defaults; the bulk import, which reads the contract, was the only path that wrote the mapping.
insight: **Two statements that write one document kind must share the converter, not each have one**: extracting the bulk import's per-entity build and calling it from both made the single form correct by construction, and the describe -> exec round trip (Unchanged) is the check that the two agree. A rewrite of an imported entity had always worked because the carry restored the mapping by name — which is why this survived: only a fresh create or a newly added attribute reached the unmapped path.
